rule: **gtest bodies are the methods gtest generates**: `TEST_F(Suite, Name) { … }` / `TEST_P` / `TYPED_TEST` define class `Suite_Name_Test` derived from the fixture `Suite` (`TEST` from `testing::Test`); the body's caller is `Suite_Name_Test#TestBody`, and bare calls and fields in it resolve through the fixture. gtest/gmock assertions (`ASSERT_*`, `EXPECT_*`, `GTEST_SKIP`, `SCOPED_TRACE`, …) are function-like macros: macro, medium. `self.m()` / `this.m()` / a bare call to a member of the enclosing type → `Type#m`. If `m` is defined only on a superclass that is in the scan, the callee is `Superclass#m`.
notes: Each TEST_F body is the TestBody method of the generated class Suite_Name_Test derived from the fixture CalcTest (Decisions 2026-11-09). Bare twice(...) resolves through the fixture: twice is defined only on the in-scan superclass CalcTest → CalcTest#twice, high. calc_ is a fixture field typed Calc → Calc#ok, high. EXPECT_EQ/ASSERT_TRUE/EXPECT_GT are gtest assertion macros: macro, medium; the calls inside their arguments are separate ordinary edges. The TEST_F(...) head itself is the declaration of the generated class and method (SPEC 'Not calls: declarations/function heads'), so it emits no edge. <gtest/gtest.h> is outside the scan; the file name calc_unittest.cpp has no path segment named test/tests, so it is in scope.
